verdict_reason: All three paper-attributed quantities are exact and I re-derived each independently. On a 120x16 float32 cloud, `effective_rank` matches a from-scratch exp(-sum p log p) on the centred RAW singular values (Roy & Vetterli 2007 Eq. (1)/Def. 1) at absolute error 7.11e-15; `participation_ratio` matches (sum lambda)^2 / sum(lambda^2) on the covariance spectrum at 7.11e-15; and `avg_cosine_similarity` matches a BRUTE-FORCE average over all N(N-1) ordered distinct pairs of the row-normalised Gram at 3.47e-18, confirming the O(ND) closed form (N||mean(unit)||^2 - 1)/(N-1) it uses instead of Ethayarajh's Monte Carlo. All three are constant across scales 1e-200 to 1e+150 (worst relative deviation 1.370e-15) and BIT-IDENTICAL under an exact zero-padding isometry d = 16 -> 128 (15.709957438519 / 14.123723461012 / -0.001424779530 before and after). I RETRACT the round-4 Opus YELLOW: it rested on `cond_number`'s numerical-rank cutoff using the CONTAINER dtype's eps, and (a) round 4 answered it -- isotropy.py:168-201 now threads the model's real precision through `source_dtype` and emits `_meta_numerical_rank_source_precision` and `_meta_cond_number_source_precision` alongside the unchanged primary, which on an exact rank-3 200x16 cloud quantised through bf16 recovers rank 3 and cond 2.223642 against a true 2.223527 (rel 5.2e-5) where the primary reads rank 16 / cond 6546.6 -- and (b) a dtype/precision convention is explicitly off the verdict axis under this brief. `cond_number` also has no source paper prescribing a truncation rule; it is a BLME diagnostic following its own documented rule. ADJUDICATION: where the two round-4 reviewers disagreed, my measurement supports gpt-5.6-sol's GREEN. The round-4 Opus YELLOW named cond_number's container-dtype tolerance, which is now disclosed with a source-precision companion, and which is a dtype question the brief places off the verdict axis in any case.
comparable_reason: `effective_rank` and `participation_ratio` are raw DIMENSION COUNTS. On a structureless iid Gaussian null at fixed N = 1200 they run 7.9892 / 7.9165 (d = 8) -> 31.8860 / 31.1256 (32) -> 126.2017 / 115.4148 (128) -> 480.5317 / 358.5887 (512), i.e. a 60x and 45x move over a 64x width range with the geometry unchanged. They also depend on the realized point count, which defaults.yaml does not pin (num_samples: 100 counts DOCUMENTS, so N varies with tokenizer and document length). `avg_cosine_similarity` is the one dimensionless output and is the defensible cross-model column. `cond_number` is additionally precision-dependent: the same model and corpus give a 22-26x different value in bf16 and fp32 because the numerical-rank cutoff follows the container dtype; the disclosed `_meta_cond_number_source_precision` companion brackets it, but the primary is not comparable across runs of different dtype.
github_reason: Read `analyze.py`'s `explore_embedding_space` in the kawine/contextual clone (the released Ethayarajh 2019 pipeline): it samples 1000 sentences, takes ONE random word occurrence from each, and averages the cosine over 1000 random pairs. The released pipeline cannot be run end to end here -- it needs AllenNLP, precomputed HDF5 embeddings and the original ~25,573-sentence corpus, while the repo ships only a 99-row sts.csv (198 contexts). I therefore re-implemented its sampler and ran BOTH on the SAME GPT-2 last-layer vectors from those 198 contexts: the released-style 1000-pair Monte Carlo gives 0.973880993 against BLME's exact all-distinct-pairs closed form 0.973191485 (delta 6.9e-04, i.e. Monte-Carlo noise), which is what validates the O(ND) identity. Roy & Vetterli 2007 released no code; that half is covered by the closed form, verified separately in geometry_collapse.
paper_reason: The released `kawine/contextual/gpt2/embedding_space_stats.json` publishes 'mean cosine similarity across words' = 0.978 for GPT-2 layer_12 (Ethayarajh 2019 Fig. 1). I ran BLME's `avg_cosine_similarity` kernel under the REFERENCE's own protocol -- one random token per context over the 198 contexts shipped in the repo's sts.csv, GPT-2 last layer -- and got 0.973191485, a relative error of -0.49%. The residual is corpus sampling, not the estimator: a transcription of the released 1000-pair Monte-Carlo sampler on the IDENTICAL vectors gives 0.973880993 (delta 6.9e-04 from BLME's exact all-pairs value), and BLME's own all-token protocol on the same texts gives 0.970521915 over 1,975 tokens. Roy & Vetterli's closed form is separately reproduced to 2.99e-16 (see geometry_collapse).
confounds_reason: `effective_rank` and `participation_ratio` ARE effective-dimension counts and rise monotonically with d_model on a no-structure null (7.99 -> 480.53 and 7.92 -> 358.59 over d = 8 -> 512 at fixed N = 1200), so any cross-model use of them is partly a width comparison. This is a property of the estimand rather than an arithmetic artifact: the same values are bit-identical under an exact zero-padding isometry (15.709957438519 / 14.123723461012 at d = 16 and d = 128), so what moves is genuine ambient-dimension use. `avg_cosine_similarity` has no such mechanism -- it is a mean of unit-vector inner products and is dimensionless -- and reproduces the published GPT-2 figure to -0.49%. `cond_number` carries a dtype channel rather than an architecture one.
defects: CODE/MODE-CONTRACT isotropy.py:~491-516: `layerwise: true` is honoured only when a populated, enabled cache is supplied and otherwise SILENTLY falls through to the last-layer route, returning 0 `layer_metrics` entries with no error and no flag. defaults.yaml pins `layerwise: false`, so it never fires in production, but the mode contract is unenforced.

PRECISION isotropy.py:~155-201: the primary `cond_number` / `_meta_numerical_rank` follow the CONTAINER dtype (collect_hidden_states casts every tensor to float32), so a bf16 production run is precision-optimistic. This is now DISCLOSED rather than hidden -- `_meta_numerical_rank_source_precision` and `_meta_cond_number_source_precision` recover rank 3 / cond 2.223642 against a true 2.223527 on an exact rank-3 cloud quantised through bf16, where the primary reads rank 16 / cond 6546.6 -- but the first-class key is still the container-precision one.

DEMOTED OUTPUT `_meta_svd_auc`: integrates the cumulative explained-variance curve over its own UNPADDED length, so an exact zero-padding isometry moves it while every promoted output is unchanged, and it underflows to NaN at a global scale of 1e-200 (it forms S**2 without the S[0] rescale the promoted keys use). The `_meta_` demotion is correct.

PROVENANCE task_metadata.py:70 credits only Ethayarajh 2019 and Roy & Vetterli 2007; `participation_ratio` has no cited source in either the code or the metadata. It is the standard inverse-participation-ratio / order-2 Hill number of the covariance spectrum and should be attributed as such -- and it is EXACTLY geometry_isoscore's `isoscore_effective_dims`, so the two must not both enter a sparse feature selection.

PROTOCOL (disclosed) Ethayarajh's released procedure samples ONE word occurrence per sentence; BLME uses every token. On the same 198 STS contexts that is 0.973191485 (one per context) vs 0.970521915 (all 1,975 tokens), so the two populations should not be pooled.
CONFIG defaults.yaml:10-12: num_samples: 100 counts DOCUMENTS, so `effective_rank`/`participation_ratio` -- which depend on N as well as d -- are not compared at a matched point count across models.
